reallyusefulribbits.guide.name: Really Useful Ribbits
reallyusefulribbits.guide.subtitle: Jobs for swamp folk
reallyusefulribbits.guide.landing: This book is an addon guide. Ribbits already have professions in the original $(item)Ribbits$() mod. This addon teaches those same frogs to fish, farm, trade, and cause trouble.$(br2)If you lose the book, craft another from an ordinary $(item)book$() and a $(item)giant lily pad$().
reallyusefulribbits.guide.cat.intro.desc: What this addon changes, and what it leaves to the original Ribbits mod.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.cat.carry.desc: How a maraca catches a ribbit in its spawn egg.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.cat.work.desc: How far ribbits look, how they share a village, and how to see their binds.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.cat.jobs.desc: What each original profession does once this addon is installed.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.welcome.1: Welcome. This guide is for players who already have $(item)Ribbits$() and want those frogs to do more than wander and play. The chapters go from catching a ribbit with a maraca, to the work radius, to each profession.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.welcome.2: You do not have to read it all at once. Open a page when a fisher will not bite, a farmer stares at dirt, or a merchant will not stop croaking.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.welcome.3: A new copy can be made at a crafting table from an ordinary book and a giant lily pad from Ribbits.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.welcome.4: If you found a bug or just want to share feedback, you can leave it here: $(l:https://github.com/Nergan/really-useful-ribbits-mod/issues)https://github.com/Nergan/really-useful-ribbits-mod/issues$(/l)
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.addon.1: This addon does $(warn)not$() add new ribbit professions. Fishers, gardeners, merchants, sorcerers and nitwits already exist in $(item)Ribbits$(). They even have their own spawn eggs. What changes is what those frogs $(job)do$() after they spawn.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.addon.2: A ribbit is still one creature. The original mod picks its profession. This addon only watches that profession and gives it work: fishing, farming, trading, luck, or chaos.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.entry.head: Maracas
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.head.1: Right-click a fisher, gardener, sorcerer or nitwit with a $(item)maraca$() from the original $(item)Ribbits$() mod. The ribbit vanishes into a spawn egg of that profession and drops whatever it was carrying. A merchant is caught only with Shift+right-click: a plain click still opens its trades, and its goods stay inside the egg. You can no longer seat a ribbit on your head.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.head.2: The egg keeps the profession, umbrella and instrument. The workplace is forgotten, and the spot where the egg is used becomes the new home. Merchant ribbits still sell maracas.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.home.1: The home point is the same one from the original Ribbits mod. A maraca no longer moves it. Catch the ribbit, carry the egg, and use the egg where the new home should be.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.home.2: Catching one grants the advancement $(thing)so I guess this is my new home now…$(). The title follows the language of the client, like the rest of this book.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.radius.1: Working ribbits scan a radius for water, farms, containers, luck, endermen and sorcerer plant-growth. The default is $(thing)64$() blocks. Several ribbits may share the same ground. They will not steal a reserved crop tile or water block from each other.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.radius.2: Scan radius, sorcerer chaos and spell points are a $(thing)SERVER$() config: Mods → Really Useful Ribbits → Config, the world file $(item)reallyusefulribbits-server.toml$(), or $(item)reallyusefulribbits-server.properties$() on Fabric. Higher chaos flattens sorcerer odds. In multiplayer only the server value matters.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.highlight: Right-click a fisher or a farmer to glow the ribbit and sprinkle particles on its container and water tile or farm. You will hear a beacon chime. No extra blocks or shulkers appear.
If that ribbit has no water, farm or container yet, it croaks in pain and angry particles appear instead. Give it time to look around, or move it closer to what it needs.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.fisherman: A fisher binds one nearby water block and one container (chest, barrel, shulker, double chest, and the like). It sits on the bank with its fishing pose and fishes like a player: splashes gather at the bobber, then it reels in. The catch is fish only. A slab in the upper half of a water block is not open water, so it will not sit and fish through it. It carries up to 4 items, and different fish all count.

A catch shows happy villager stars, the fishing bobber splash, and a quiet orb ping. The fisher sits on the water's edge. Fish dropped nearby with $(thing)Q$() are picked up. At 4 items it stands up, walks to the container, deposits normal stacks, and goes back to the water.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.farmer.1: A gardener binds one connected farm and one container. The farm is every touching patch of farmland (including Farmer's Delight), soul sand, sugar-cane base, crop standing in water or on mud, or bush crop within 128 blocks. Sweet berry bushes and other prickly bushes are left alone. It takes seeds by the stack and plants the nearest empty soil. Soul sand only takes nether wart. It harvests melons and pumpkins next to their stems. Bone meal, from the bag, the container, or the ground, speeds up its own plants. Harvest goes into the container; seeds and bone meal stay in the bag. Inventory is four slots of 64.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.farmer.2: It works like a little straw golem: harvest ripe crops first (pumpkins and melons as the fruit blocks, not the stems), then replant, then walk the produce to its chest. Sugar cane is cut, never planted. It never tramples farmland. It walks up to the chest; it will not insert or take items from across the field. Thrown seeds and crops within a few blocks are picked up. Crops that harvest on a right-click, such as Farmer's Delight tomatoes, are gathered that way. Watering is short and infrequent: it wets farmland and sometimes coaxes glow berries onto vines. It only tills a dirt hole boxed in on all four sides.
A merchant has 27 slots of 256. It starts with a few random goods plus 256 emeralds and 256 amethyst shards. It visits other traders and copies the items they sell, then builds up to twice as many amethyst sell offers as a typical stall — an average of the shops it has seen.
Happy villager stars appear when the stall refreshes. Glow particles follow it while it chases a player. Right-click opens its offers. Each item type appears only once. It always walks at 1.5× speed.
Right-click a sorcerer with an $(item)amethyst shard$() — the shard is spent — and it looks at you, then rolls a spell that can actually happen. Every spell has points in the $(thing)SERVER$() config: its chance is its points divided by the sum of all points, and 0 turns it off. Common rolls: growth, weather, a diamond rain, lightning that spares the frog, a fire ring, a trip to a structure, a random structure built nearby, summoned mobs or tamed pets.

States stay after death until their timer runs out: an effect, upside-down, size, max health, a morph, a silly nickname, a $(thing)Super Secret Settings$() shader, inverted controls, $(thing)VVVVVV$() gravity on the jump key, ghast fireballs or lightning from an empty hand, and creative flight. The server config sets each duration in seconds; -1 lasts until something removes it. Spectator defaults to one hour and the bedrock room to five minutes. The time left is shown on the left of the screen, even for states the game does not list as effects. Milk still clears ordinary effects. Everything else comes off only when you feed the sorcerer an $(item)enchanted golden apple$() ($(thing)Get this off me!$()).

Rarer rolls: a giant glowing phantom ($(thing)Foma, is that you?$()), a tamed cat fifty times bigger ($(thing)Musya?!$()), an hour as a spectator, a blast ten times stronger than TNT, a random dimension, a rare morph ($(thing)hexed :($()) — only humanoid mobs can still place, break and open things — or a bedrock room around you for five minutes ($(thing)Walled In!$()).

Disasters: an ender dragon, fireballs from the top of the world, a lake of lava over the frog, and corrupted generation of every new chunk — the apple lifts that one too. Just as rare as the corruption is $(thing)delete the world$(): a warden a hundred times bigger with 10 000 health that hunts players anywhere. While it lives the night never ends, the sky turns blood-red and sculk spreads. Whoever kills it gets creative mode.
Clicking empty-handed makes the frog angry. Endermen flee from it. Chaos in the server config pushes the odds toward an even roll; it is 0 by default.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.nitwit.1: A nitwit still applies $(thing)Luck$() inside the scan radius. It also picks up loot on the ground: it walks to the item and takes it. The bag is 27 slots of 64.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.nitwit.2: Once it is carrying something, it sometimes walks up to a player and tosses the items the way a player drops them with $(thing)Q$(). It will not fish, farm, or trade. A maraca catches it in a spawn egg.
